newsitem.title: USA: U.S. NICKEL SLUGGISH DESPITE SUPPLY DISRUPTIONS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. NICKEL SLUGGISH DESPITE SUPPLY DISRUPTIONS.

text.p: Despite a strike at a major Canadian mine and production problems at Europe's largest smelter, the U.S. physical nickel market has been sluggish, adding up to what many traders perceive to be poor fundamentals.

Since union workers at Falconbridge Inc's Sudbury complex walked off the job on Aug 1, the benchmark three-month price has fallen from a high of $7,580 a tonne ($3.43 a lb) to its current level of $6,700 a tonne ($3.06 a lb) at the close of the last kerb, a 13.1 percent drop.
Outokumpu Oy's Harjavalta smelter is also down for maintenance following an explosion in late June that injured three.
"Falconbridge is on strike. Outokumpu is down. And the price is down $900," one trader said with a chuckle. "It comes down to the fact that there's no demand."
Sudbury produces 45,000 tonnes of nickel annually, while Harjavalta's annual capacity is 40,000 tonnes. Together they account for 11.6 percent of Western world production.
"It's usually slow this time of year," the trader said. "We're hoping that demand returns in September, but I couldn't guarantee it."
Other traders say producers of stainless steel, which accounts for two-thirds of nickel consumption, have been regular buyers, but demand has been outpaced by supply.

"There's too much nickel around," a New York merchant said. "Stainless steel production is moving along at a good pace. The problem is on the supply side. The market doesn't care about Falconbridge and Outokumpu because there's plenty of metal around."
He called for prices to trade in a range of $6,500-$7,500 a tonne for the remainder of the year. "Other than technical short-covering rallies, I'm not optimistic for higher prices at all."

"Russian imports into the U.S. started arriving a little earlier than people were used to," explained another dealer. "But still June and July were pretty good months from the stainless people. But in August, they've been laying low. We've only been hearing from the foundries and alloy makers."
Nickel premiums have widened slightly to 9.00-12.00 cents over LME cash. "But you have to take that number with a grain of salt, because there hasn't been a lot of business done."
The bid opening from U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center on Thursday is expected to offer clues as to the next move for premiums.
